recipes.name: Simple Sweet and Spicy Chicken Wraps
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into thin strips

steps.text: Make the sauce: Mix mayonnaise, cucumber, honey, cayenne pepper, and black pepper together in a bowl until smooth. Cover and refrigerate until needed.

Make the wraps: Heat olive oil in a skillet on medium-high heat. Add chicken strips; cook and stir until they start to turn golden and are no longer pink in the middle, about 8 minutes. Stir in salsa, honey, and cayenne pepper. Reduce the heat to medium-low; simmer, stirring occasionally, until flavors have blended, about 5 minutes.
Stack tortillas, 4 at a time, in a microwave oven and heat until warm and pliable, 20 to 30 seconds per batch.
Spread each tortilla with 1 tablespoon mayonnaise-cucumber sauce, top with a layer of spinach, and arrange about 1/2 cup of the chicken mixture on top.

Fold the bottom of each tortilla up about 2 inches, and start rolling from the right side. When wrap is halfway rolled, fold the top of the tortilla down, enclosing the filling, and continue rolling to make a tight, compact cylinder.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Sweet and Spicy Chicken Wraps
raw_recipe.description: This salsa chicken wrap has a creamy sauce made with mayo, honey, and cucumber for a sweet and spicy spin that will shake up your lunch routine.

video.description: Change up your chicken routine with this excellently flavored spin on a chicken wrap. Begin by making a sauce of mayo, finely chopped seedless cucumber, honey, cayenne pepper, black pepper and olive oil. Then cook chicken breast strips over medium-high heat. Stir in salsa, honey and cayenne pepper and simmer until flavors have developed. Spread cucumber sauce inside warm flour tortillas, then top with baby spinach leaves and chicken mixture, and finally, eat!

review.reviewBody: Absolutely delish! My husband kept snitching the chicken out of the pan. I subbed in plain yogurt for the mayo because I don't like the taste or texture of mayo, but didn't change anything else. This will go on my list of summer menus.

Simply delicious!I halved the recipe since there was only three of us eating, I had a three grilled chicken breast from the night before so I was able to prepare this in very little time, I used whole wheat tortillas and lettuce instead of spinach(that's what I had) other than that followed the recipe exactly. When done they looked delicious and tasted delicious. Thanks for sumitting your recipe! Something that we will be making often, especially during the summer.

This is very light and delicious! I made it exactly as written (except using spinach wraps) and it was a huge hit with the family! I did add some chopped cucumber, green onion, tomato and grated cheddar cheese to a couple of them as requested by a family member and that was wonderful too. We will definitely be making this again! update: I found that the leftover chicken was kind of dry so I tried shredding the chicken and adding some water before refrigerating and that made the flavor even better the next day both cold and reheated! YUM!

I followed the recipe exactly as stated, with a minor change, and a finishing adjustment. For the change: I didn't start with fresh chicken, I had a single leftover baked chicken breast, and about 2/3 of leftover Sam's Club rotisserie chicken. I cut all the chicken into small cubes and combined it in the skillet. Not a big change, but worth mentioning in case anyone else as inexperienced as I am is wondering. For the finishing adjustment: I sprinkled blue cheese crumbles inside the wrap, and it was fantastic. The blue cheese added just enough 'whatever' to counter the spicy of the wrap, and without it, I don't think I would have added this into our rotation. A couple of minor notes: The wrap is borderline "too spicy", but I liked the bit of extra heat. Also, oddly enough, the smell of the finished and constructed wrap (without the blue cheese) somehow made it less appealing to my youngest child, and I agree somewhat - the chicken didn't smell as tantalizing as I expected when it was cooking, but perhaps that's due to the spices/herbs used in the leftover pieces.
Phenomenal recipe as is, the second time I did add lime juice to the chicken as I cooked it and julienned the cucumber. thank you, the whole family loved it!

These make a perfect lunch on a warm day! Now since it is approaching bikini season, i somewhat deviated from the original recipe. I used greek yogurt instead of mayo, added shredded carrots & grilled the chicken before cooking it with the salsa. It turned out great!

So quick, easy and yummy! I usually make a double batch, which yields about 12-13 large (burrito size tortilla) wraps. I actually make double the cuke sauce for a single batch, and I quadruple it for a double batch. The cayenne in the chicken/salsa mixture is spicy enough on its own, so I usually use half the amount of cayenne listed for the cuke sauce. Also, I shred the cuke like I do for tzatziki and squeeze the excess juice from it. We much prefer the thicker consistency of sour cream vs mayo for the sauce, but it works with either. This recipe is very adaptable since you can season the chicken any way you like (cumin, garlic, a little chili powder) or even use rotisserie chicken. Ditto the sauce. I like to add a touch of salt, squirt of lime and some cilantro. We like to add some chopped romaine along w/the spinach for crunch, too.

This is a very easy tasty quick dinner! My partner loved it, too. I replaced a half mayo with plain yogurt to make it lighter that worked very well. The mixture of the mayo (and yogurt in my way), honey, cayenne pepper, black pepper and diced cucumber is a wonderful sauce. I will use it for other recipe, too. I added pan sauteed sugar snap that is a wonderful addition to give it a crispy fresh punch.

If I make this again, I would cook the chicken differently. I really didn't like the chicken cooked with salsa. It didn't brown and looked and tasted blah. I would season the chicken (maybe a sweet and spicy rub) and grill it, then cut into strips. I did like the sauce and overall this was a tasty meal.

This is SO delicious! I made a few changes though. I used sour cream instead of mayo & cut back on the cayenne pepper (was TOO hot the first time as-is). I also added avacado on top! I like to double the sauce portion to make a little extra since the sauce is so good!

Very good and very easy for a quick, weeknight meal. I omitted the cayenne pepper altogether from this recipe to make it kid-friendly for our 4 year-old. I added some garlic and onion powders to the mayo/cucumber mixture. As a family preference, I shredded the chicken and added a handful of shredded cheddar cheese along with the salsa and honey. Used mother-in-law's homemade tortillas as the "wraps" and subbed shredded lettuce in mine.....hubby liked the spinach. I also added a bit more shredded cheese to our wraps. Thanks for this delicious submission....a definite regular in our summer meal rotation!
Very tasty. The cool cucumber sauce goes perfectly with the slightly spicy chicken. Would make again.
Really good, really easy.
The most GOATed recipe ever
Delicious flavor combo of the sweet and spicy. I added chipotle powder and smoked paprika to enhance the flavor even more. Will make again!
Amazing

Great, unique but easy wrap/meal/recipe! Did not change a single thing and we loved them! If I would make an addition, it MIGHT be adding some sliced jalapeños and/or green onions. However, as is, these wraps are perfect for those hectic weeknights or a quick Saturday lunch! Will absolutely make again! Thanks Nuclear Rich! This recipe rocked!
Followed the recipe to the tee. Loved it! The only thing that I did extra was I added cheddar cheese and some cilantro for the wife (I hate cilantro, tastes like soap) will definitely make again
Absolutely addicting!
so awesome and easy. i loved it
